pages.learnerAction: Answer the tutor’s relevant question, then ask the tutor the related reciprocal question.
pages.tutorAction: Answer genuinely, react to the learner, and follow the most interesting detail without forcing the pattern.
pages.targetOrPrompt: Exact Tutor question: “When you get lost, do you ask someone or check a map first? Why?” Exact learner reciprocal question: “What do you do first when you get lost?”
pages.learningTarget: Answer the personal or preference question “When you get lost, do you ask someone or check a map first? Why?”, then reverse the direction of the conversation by asking the tutor “What do you do first when you get lost?”
pages.pedagogicalValue: “When you get lost, do you ask someone or check a map first? Why?” stands alone without the lesson frame and invites a real answer; “What do you do first when you get lost?” creates a genuine second direction instead of ending after one response.
pages.failureDiagnosis: If “When you get lost, do you ask someone or check a map first? Why?” were a disguised scenario-production command, or if the learner never asked “What do you do first when you get lost?”, this would be another one-way pattern exercise rather than reciprocal free talk.
